title: backoff-weirdness-playbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal playbook for investigating weird 401/429 behavior we've been seeing from a handful of customer sessions. Keep this as my working scratchpad: commands tried, raw snippets, hypotheses, and next actions. Not polished — notes to self.

Summary of problem observed:
- Sporadic 401s and 429s coming from the hosted API for the same API key within a short window.
- Some sessions see a flurry of 401s for a few seconds then normal traffic; others see steady 429s with Retry-After that are inconsistent with quota numbers reported in dashboard.
- Affects mobile app customer X and internal stress-test harness.

What I have repro'd so far (shell + curl):
1) Minimal repro to see 401 transient:
   curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test-transient" \n     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n     -d '{"model":"rwd-medium","input":"hello"}' \n     https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
   -> HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
   Response body: {"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"key not found"}
   Headers: x-request-id: req_01F5X.., server: rwd-api/2.1

2) Repeat same curl 3s later with identical key -> HTTP/1.1 200 OK; body: {"output":"hi"}
   Hypothesis: rotation/replication lag in key store or caching layer.

3) Load run -> consistent 429s:
   for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{url_effective}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-loadtest" -d '{"model":"rwd-small","input":"x"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate & done
   Observed ~70% 200, ~30% 429 across the run, with Retry-After sometimes absent.

Observed headers in 429 cases (example):
- HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
- x-request-id: req_01F6A..
- retry-after: 3
- x-rate-limit-limit: 1000
- x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
- x-rate-limit-reset: 1690000000
But dashboard shows remaining > 0 at same timestamp.

Server log snippets (pulled via prod-stdout, redacted):
[2025-08-13T09:12:01.342Z] request=req_01F6A user=acct_88 route=/v1/generate key=sk-loadtest status=429 reason=burst_quota_exceeded token_count=42 node=gw-12
[2025-08-13T09:12:01.345Z] quota-check: window=60s limit=1000 used=850 backend=quota-svc-3 cache=miss
[2025-08-13T09:12:01.347Z] quota-service: incremented counter -> new=851 (local-cache-ttl=1s)

Interesting — quota-service shows cache=miss then new counts jump; dashboard uses periodic rollups and sometimes lags behind local quota caches (explains mismatch).

Edge conditions / patterns noticed:
- 401s often spike right after a key rotation event from keys-service (owner mentioned a key "rollover" job at ~09:10). Repro: create ephemeral key, flip active pointer, then hammer with old and new key in quick succession -> old key yields 401 for ~2s then recovers.
- 429s where Retry-After absent appear when the router short-circuits before quota-service returns (fast-fail path). Those 429s correlate with high CPU on gw nodes and elevated latency to quota-svc.
- Mobile clients occasionally retry aggressively (no jitter/backoff) causing cascade of 429s.

Commands & probes used to gather telemetry:
- curl -v to capture headers + x-request-id
- httpie for readable output: http POST https://api... Authorization:"Bearer sk-..." model=rwd-small input=x
- ab/hey/palp: hey -n 1000 -c 40 -m POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-loadtest' -D headers.txt -d '{"model":"rwd-small","input":"x"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
- tcpdump on gw-12: sudo tcpdump -i eth0 port 443 -w gw12-20250813.pcap (to check client IP clustering)
- curl to keys-service: curl -s https://keys.internal/active -> JSON with pointer to key id (sometimes lags)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Key rotation race: active pointer flips before caches (edge caches, gw) have invalidated -> short window of 401s for old key. Evidence: timing with rotation job.
2) Local quota caches inconsistent with central dashboard: GW nodes maintain local counters with short TTL, causing apparent mismatch (dashboard is eventual). Evidence: log "cache=miss" then increments.
3) Fast-fail path for quota-check returns 429 without Retry-After when quota-svc times out or is overloaded. Evidence: retry-after absent + high CPU + quota-svc latency observed.
4) SDK/client retry behavior exacerbating the problem (no jitter -> synchronized retries). Evidence: mobile client logs show back-to-back retries with no exponential jitter.
5) Key scope mismatch: some keys limited to certain routes, causing 401 on route mismatch — less likely but checkable by key metadata.

Things I tried that didn't help (and notes):
- Increasing bandwidth of test runner (not root cause).
- Forcing connection: close header — small change in connection reuse but no elimination of 401s.
- Shortening local-cache-ttl in staging quota-svc to 100ms: reduced 429 variance in staging but not fully eliminating; suggests race window is small.

Quick checklist to run next when reproducing:
- Capture x-request-id and then query logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/?q=req_01F6A
- Pull quota-svc traces around timestamp: /traces?svc=quota-svc&from=2025-08-13T09:11:58&to=2025-08-13T09:12:05
- Check keys-service events: /keys/audit?from=2025-08-13T09:09:00&to=2025-08-13T09:13:00 for rotation jobs
- Re-run test with environmental variable SDK_BACKOFF=off and with SDK_BACKOFF=jittered to compare.
- Run single-gw isolated test (pin to gw-13 only) to see if cross-node cache inconsistency is the culprit.

Temporary mitigations considered:
- Add a short grace period post-key-rotation where the old key is accepted for ~5s (cheap fix but masks underlying cache invalidation).
- Make quota-svc respond with Retry-After in fast-fail path (improves client behavior).
- Add jittered retry guidance to mobile SDK docs (client-side mitigation).

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why do some 401 spikes recover in <1s without a key change? Are there bg GC jobs or cache evictions?
- Can we make dashboard near-real-time to avoid confusion? (not urgent for production but helpful for debugging).
- Is any CDN edge caching auth result? Need to inspect CDN config for any key auth caching TTL.

Action items (me):
- [ ] Reproduce in isolated environment with controlled key-rotation and single gw. (priority: high)
- [ ] Ask keys-service owners for rotation schedule and to add audit logs with timestamps of pointer flips. (priority: med) — ping @Daniel
- [ ] Prototype short grace period for old keys in keys-service (low risk). (priority: low)
- [ ] Add Retry-After on fast-fail 429 path and ship to staging. (priority: med)
- [ ] Draft short mobile-SDK guidance about exponential backoff + jitter. (priority: med)

Notes to self: keep this doc as ephemeral scratch; when hypothesis converge, move cleaned reproduction steps and concrete fixes into shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/ and create a Jira RL ticket for the code change.

Raw dump of a particularly interesting request (redacted):
Request headers:
  :method: POST
  :path: /v1/generate
  host: api.redwood.example
  authorization: Bearer sk-loadtest
  content-type: application/json
  x-client-version: mobile-android-3.2.1
  x-forwarded-for: 54.23.12.99

Response captured:
  HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
  x-request-id: req_01F6A9aB
  x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
  retry-after: (missing)
  date: Wed, 13 Aug 2025 09:12:01 GMT
  content-type: application/json
  body: {"error":"rate_limited","message":"quota exceeded"}

If I get time: instrument gw to log "pre-quota latency" and "quota-svc-latency" separately so we can see how often gw is returning fast-fail vs waiting. Also check client SDK versions in mobile logs — older SDK lacked jitter and had aggressive immediate retries.

End of notes.
